Do this at home, before Day 1. If you arrive with the accounts created and the programs installed, Day 1 goes to building instead of waiting for confirmation emails. If something fails, come anyway: from 08:20 to 09:00 on Day 1 there is a setup check, and neighbors help neighbors.

**Golden rule.** If a command answers with an error in red, do not continue to the next step. Copy the whole error and bring it to class, or paste it into [claude.ai](https://claude.ai) with: *"What does this mean and how do I fix it on Mac / Windows?"*

## The pieces, one sentence each

| Piece | What it is | Think of it as |
|---|---|---|
| **VS Code** | The editor where the files of your web live | Your desk |
| **Claude Code** | An assistant that reads, writes and runs code in your project | A very capable colleague working next to you |
| **Git and GitHub** | Every version of your files, kept and backed up | A drive with the full history of changes |
| **Vercel** | The service that publishes your web at a public address | The shop where you open the doors |
| **Node.js** | The engine your web runs on while you build it | The kitchen behind the shop |

## What it costs

| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Claude **Pro** plan, paid by each student | About USD 20 a month. Claude Code does not work on the free plan. You need it active on Day 1 and from Day 2 to Day 3; keeping it between them lets you practice. |
| GitHub, Vercel Hobby, Supabase Free | Free |

Confirm the current price at [claude.ai](https://claude.ai) before you pay; prices change.

## Part 1 · Accounts (15 minutes)

Use **the same email** for all of them. A personal email you will keep after the MBA is best.

```{=html}
<ul class="vc-checklist" id="setup-accounts">
<li><span><strong>Claude</strong> at <a href="https://claude.ai">claude.ai</a>, with the <strong>Pro</strong> plan or higher.</span></li>
<li><span><strong>GitHub</strong> at <a href="https://github.com/signup">github.com/signup</a>. Free.</span></li>
<li><span><strong>Vercel</strong> at <a href="https://vercel.com/signup">vercel.com/signup</a>. Choose <strong>Continue with GitHub</strong> and the <strong>Hobby</strong> plan (free).</span></li>
<li><span>Write five lines about <strong>your idea</strong>: what the web is for, who visits it, what they should do there, two sites whose look you like, and what you do not want.</span></li>
</ul>
```

## Part 2 · Programs (30 minutes)

Everything happens in a **terminal**, a window where you type instructions to your computer. On a Mac: ⌘ + Space, type `Terminal`, Enter. On Windows: Start menu, type `PowerShell`, open it. To run a command, copy it, paste it into the terminal and press Enter. After each program there is a **test**: do not move on if it fails.

### 1. VS Code

Download it from [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com) and install it like any program. On a Mac, drag it into **Applications**; do not open it from Downloads. Open it, and in the top menu choose **Terminal → New Terminal**. From here on, use that terminal.

**Test:** `code --version` shows a number. On a Mac, if it says `command not found: code`: press ⌘ + Shift + P, type *Shell Command: Install 'code' command in PATH*, and press Enter.

### 2. Git

```{=html}
<div class="vc-prompt"><div class="vc-prompt-h">In the terminal · Mac</div><div class="vc-prompt-b">xcode-select --install</div></div>
```

A window opens: accept and install, which takes a few minutes. **Windows:** download it from [git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/download/win) and keep every default option. Then tell Git who you are, with the same email as GitHub:

```{=html}
<div class="vc-prompt"><div class="vc-prompt-h">In the terminal · Mac and Windows</div><div class="vc-prompt-b">git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "your-email@example.com"</div></div>
```

**Test:** `git --version` shows something like `git version 2.4x`.

### 3. Node.js

Go to [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org), download the **LTS** version (the recommended one, not "Current") and install it with the default options. Then **close and reopen VS Code**, or its terminal will not see the new program.

**Test:** `node -v` and `npm -v` both show numbers; Node must be 22 or higher.

**Windows only:** if `npm -v` answers *running scripts is disabled on this system*, run `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned`, answer Y, and reopen the terminal.

### 4. Claude Code

```{=html}
<div class="vc-prompt"><div class="vc-prompt-h">In the terminal · Mac</div><div class="vc-prompt-b">curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash</div></div>
<div class="vc-prompt"><div class="vc-prompt-h">In PowerShell · Windows</div><div class="vc-prompt-b">irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex</div></div>
```

Close and reopen the terminal, then type `claude`. The first time, it asks you to sign in: choose your **Claude account (Pro or higher)**, accept in the browser, and come back to the terminal.

**Test:** inside Claude Code, type `/status`. Your account appears. Type `/exit` to leave. Running `claude` once in the terminal also sets up Anthropic's official plugin catalog, which you use on Sunday.

**The VS Code extension.** In VS Code, open **Extensions** (the squares icon on the left, or ⌘/Ctrl + Shift + X), search for **Claude Code** published by **Anthropic**, and install it. Open any file: a Spark icon (✻) appears at the top right of the editor, and clicking it opens Claude in a panel next to your files. The panel and the terminal are the same Claude. In class we use the panel, and the terminal when we need it.

### Where your projects live

Create a folder called **Proyectos** in your user folder: `/Users/your-name/Proyectos` on a Mac, `C:\Users\your-name\Proyectos` on Windows.

**Not** on the Desktop, in Documents, iCloud, OneDrive or Google Drive. Those folders sync and "optimize" files while Claude is writing them, and they have deleted whole projects. Your backup is GitHub, not the sync folder.

## A warm-up that saves time on Sunday (5 to 10 minutes)

Thirty laptops downloading the same web project on the room's wifi is slow. Download it once at home, so that on Sunday most of it comes from your laptop. In the terminal, one line at a time:

```{=html}
<div class="vc-prompt"><div class="vc-prompt-h">In the terminal · Mac</div><div class="vc-prompt-b">mkdir -p ~/Proyectos && cd ~/Proyectos
npx --yes create-next-app@latest calentamiento --yes</div></div>
<div class="vc-prompt"><div class="vc-prompt-h">In the terminal · Windows</div><div class="vc-prompt-b">mkdir $HOME\Proyectos -Force; cd $HOME\Proyectos
npx --yes create-next-app@latest calentamiento --yes</div></div>
```

It ends with *Success! Created calentamiento*. You can delete that folder afterwards; it was only a rehearsal.

## The five tests

```{=html}
<ul class="vc-checklist" id="setup-tests">
<li><code>code --version</code> shows a number.</li>
<li><code>git config --global user.email</code> shows the email of your GitHub account.</li>
<li><code>node -v</code> shows 22 or higher.</li>
<li><code>claude</code> opens, and inside it <code>/status</code> shows your account (then <code>/exit</code>).</li>
<li>In VS Code, the Spark icon (✻), or <strong>✻ Claude Code</strong> in the status bar at the bottom, opens the Claude Code panel.</li>
</ul>
```

## On a work laptop

A laptop managed by your employer may block installing programs, or block the Claude Code installer. Try at home first. If it is blocked, bring a personal laptop, or ask your IT team for permission before Sunday. Do not work around your employer's security controls.

## Before Day 2

By Sunday 10 January 2027, create a free [Supabase](https://supabase.com/dashboard) account with **Continue with GitHub**. Day 2 connects it to Claude to give your web a database and a login. The free plan pauses a project after a week without use; a click on **Restore** in its dashboard brings it back. Anything else Day 2 needs is listed on its class page.

## If you could not finish

Come to Day 1 anyway: the setup check from 08:20 is for exactly this. If you will miss Day 1, write to [sebastian.azocarm@usm.cl](mailto:sebastian.azocarm@usm.cl) before it. Nobody is graded on this guide.
